title: High-Contrast Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack for Dual-Bandpass
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic Si/SiO2 quarter-wave stack with 10 layer pairs can achieve simultaneous high transmittance at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while maintaining stopbands at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm through natural Bragg reflection harmonics.
design_principle: High index contrast (Δn ~ 2.4 for Si/SiO2 in mid-IR) creates wide stopbands with fewer layers. Quarter-wave optical thickness at the geometric mean of passbands produces transmission windows at harmonic positions that can align with the two gas absorption bands.
proposed_topology: Air | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Si | SiO2 | Daimon-20 substrate, 20 coating layers total
design_variables: individual thicknesses of all 20 coating layers
manufacturing_considerations: Si and SiO2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Daimon-20 substrate requires low-temperature deposition compatibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for periodic multilayers
Bragg reflection condition for stopband formation
High index contrast reduces required layer count per L01
expected_advantages: Fewer layers needed due to high Δn
Natural harmonic transmission windows may align with dual passbands
known_risks: Quarter-wave design may not precisely align both passbands simultaneously
Stopband edges may not match required 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm exactly
Si absorption in mid-IR may reduce peak transmittance
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer periodic stack on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate under air normal incidence. Stack structure: Air | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | Si | SiO2 (Kischkat) | CaF2 (Daimon-20). Vary all 20 coating layer thicknesses independently. Target high transmittance at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm. Target low transmittance at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm. No metal layers. Materials: si, SiO2 (Kischkat). Substrate: CaF2 (Daimon-20). Maximum 24 layers respected.
